summary.value: Irregularly shaped, water-soaked leaf spots that appear angular because they are bounded by the leaf veins; bacteria may ooze from the spots in droplets that dry to a white residue, the area later turns gray and dies, and dead tissue often tears away leaving large irregular holes. Fruit lesions are smaller, circular, and superficial.
summary.quote: The leaf spot is irregularly shaped with a water-soaked appearance; bounded by the leaf veins the shapes of spots are angular. Bacteria may ooze from the spots in droplets, which dry to a white residue. The water-soaked area later turns gray and dies. Often, dead tissue is torn away from the healthy portion, leaving large, irregular holes. Water-soaked spots on fruit are smaller than on leaves, and they are circular.

diagnostic_features.value: The spots expand until limited by larger veins, which gives them an angular appearance; under humid conditions the water-soaked spots are covered by a white exudate (bacterial ooze) that dries to a thin, white crust on or adjacent to the spot on the underleaf surface; as spots dry they tear away leaving large, irregular holes.
diagnostic_features.quote: The spots expand until they are limited by larger veins, which give the spots an angular appearance. Under humid conditions, water-soaked spots are covered by a white exudate, which eventually dries to form a thin, white crust on or adjacent to the spot on the underleaf surface.

value: Plant certified, pathogen-free (clean, bacteria-free) seed; if saving seed, do not collect seed from infected plants.
Plant resistant/tolerant varieties (many resistant cucumber varieties are available).
Hot water seed treatment can remove some, but not all, bacteria (not fully effective alone).
Rotate out of cucurbits for 2 or more years (do not grow cucurbits in the same field more than once every three or four years) and avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization.
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers; if watering by hand, water at the base of the plant.
Do not cultivate, harvest, or work in plants when leaves are wet, and stay out of wet, infected fields.
Remove and destroy infected fruit and vines at the end of the season; in large fields till in or plow under infected debris to speed decomposition.
Apply copper-based bactericides early (e.g., fixed-copper products, Badge SC, Cueva, Kocide, Previsto) at first sign of disease; sprays are not effective once disease is severe.
Apply Actigard 50WG (Group P1) at 0.5 to 1 oz/A on 7-day intervals.
Tank-mix the recommended bactericide with effective fungicides to also protect against fungal diseases.
treatments.quote: Buy clean seed from a reputable source. If saving seed, do not collect seed from infected plants. Hot water treatment can remove some, but not all, bacteria. Rotate vegetables ... Use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers if possible. Do not work in plants when leaves are wet. ... Copper can slow the spread of disease if used early. Sprays are not effective once disease is severe.

summary.quote: Downy mildew causes angular, yellow to brown lesions on top of the leaves that are restricted by leaf veins ( Figure 1 ). This downy growth is masses of pathogen spores called sporangia, which can be seen in the field with a 20X hand lens.

value: Plant early in the season to escape high disease pressure

Scout plants often and remove infected plants
Sign up for and monitor the Cucurbit Downy Mildew IPM Pipe (ipmPIPE) website for outbreaks and report any outbreaks to alert others

Protect the crop with fungicides, applied before disease develops; before disease appears apply at 7-day intervals for cucumbers and 10-day intervals for other cucurbits, and after detection at 5-day intervals for cucumbers and 7-day intervals for other cucurbits
